current_answer: As of 20 October 2026, public evidence reviewed here does not establish broad capability decline across popular AI models. BridgeBench reports Claude Opus 5.5 at 105.8 on 16 October relative to its first tracked session, up from 95.7 on 9 October and within its own 90–110 band. Its composite mixes correctness, output tokens, and cost, so an index shift is not a pure accuracy measure; its private task set does not represent all Claude use. LiveNerf reports no change in its first complete 10-day follow-up window on a narrow 78-item reasoning-and-math panel (+0.007 ± 0.018 score units; 780 attempts in both baseline and window). Its 17 October update had only five of ten days in the second window, so the preregistered two-window persistence rule was not yet decided. These scoped results are useful counterweights to anecdotal decline reports, but do not rule out smaller or workflow-specific losses. For a completed answer that seems weaker, replay the same safe task with model, surface, effort, tools, context, and scoring held or recorded; investigate access, routing, product state, and outages separately when no answer arrives.

catalogue_card.question: Do public Opus 5.5 trackers show the same decline?
catalogue_card.text: Not on the data checked: BridgeBench is inside its own composite band and LiveNerf reports no change in its first full window. Their panels and baselines differ; neither settles performance on your workflow.

summary: No broad capability decline is established by this public-source review.
BridgeBench reports Opus 5.5 at 105.8 relative to its first tracked session on 16 October, still within its stated 90–110 band.
BridgeBench’s composite includes correctness, output tokens, and cost; the result page does not expose each component.
LiveNerf reports no change in its first complete 10-day window on a separate 78-item reasoning/math panel; its second window was incomplete as of 17 October.
Different trackers do not pool into a universal quality result; small or workflow-specific changes remain possible.
Replay the same safe task with settings held for completed-answer concerns; check access and route separately for failed requests.
uncertainty: BridgeBench tests a private 50-task suite with three attempts per task and a composite; its report omits component scores and does not generalize to every task, surface, or account.
BridgeBench defines its reference as the first tracked session; the public materials reviewed do not establish that it is the provider launch-day state.
The LiveNerf result covers a calibrated 78-item reasoning/math panel, not consumer workflows; its preregistered second follow-up window was incomplete as of 17 October.
LiveNerf uses a different task set, score, baseline, and collection method from BridgeBench, so the two series are not a direct replication or pooled estimate.
The recent community posts are self-selected anecdotes; they do not establish incidence, broad decline, or willingness to pay.
The read-only analytics broker was unavailable, so reader actions, repeat use, discovery, and commercial outcomes were not measured.
freshness_note: Reviewed 20 October 2026. Two distinct Opus 5.5 public trackers provide scoped counterevidence; neither is a controlled test across popular models or all user workflows.
